To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
A2A adeno-sine receptors expressed on T cells mediate protection against renal ischemia-reperfus-ion injury and that IFN-γ produced by CD4+ T cells is an important mediator of injury.
CD4+ T cells contribute to renal injury and that A2AR expressed by CD4+ cells are involved in mediating tissue protection from renal IRI.
A2A adrenosine receptors (A2AARs) are expressed in T cells, and that A2ARs expressed in CD4 T cells mediate the renal protective effects of A2AR agonists in renal IRI.
In summary, our research is concerned with
identifying mechanisms of tissue protection and developing therapeutic approaches for renal IRI.
the role of adenosine 2AR in the regulation of the immune response in the kidney.
the role of adenosine 2a receptor (A2A)-mediated protection from ischemia reperfusion injury in the kidney.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
A2A receptor-mediated protection from IRI is mediated by CD4+ AAR cells and IFN- γ is the key effector cytokine.
CD4+ cells expressing A2AR and producing IFN-γ are important mediators of renal IRI.

A2A adenoisne receptor (A2A AR)-expressing bone-marrow-derived cells (BMDCs) contribute to the renal protection afforded by A2A AR agonists in renal IRI, but the role of CD+ T cells and IFN- γ in the renal protective effect remains to be defined.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the A2AR expressed on T cells is important in mediating the protective effect of the A2AR agonist in renal ischemia reperfusion injury (RI) and that this effect is mediated by IFN-γ.
A2ARs in CD4+ T-cells are important for tissue protection in the setting of IRI and that the protective effect of the A2AR is mediated in part through IFN-γ.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the A2A agonism is not the only mechanism by which A2A agonistic drugs are protective.
